physicalNotes: Radius 0.18734977 Jupiter radii from Filomeno et al. 2026 (2026A&A...708A..90F), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..90F/abstract): 13,394 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0286318 Jupiter masses (Filomeno et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026A&A...708A..90F), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..90F/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): P 6.1842161 d
sources.shape: Filomeno et al. 2026 (2026A&A...708A..90F), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname FILOMENO_ET_AL_2026): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.05921 au and stellar radius 0.639 solar radii; Filomeno et al. 2026 (2026A&A...708A..90F), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname FILOMENO_ET_AL_2026): inclination 89.88 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2458848.6877 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 4 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
